text:
zach: FYI started seeing a spike in GPU attach failures in eu-central at ~03:02 UTC. pods stuck 'Attaching volume' and attach latency p95 jumped to ~120ms.

infra-bot: alert: nvme_write_latency_p95 > 100ms (eu-central) — firing at 03:05 UTC

priya: can you paste the iostat / nvme stats?

zach: grab: `iostat -x 1 3` showed avg await for nvme0n1 ~ 85ms, util ~98%. `nvme top` shows high active writes + background GC threads ramping.

arun: did we just run snapshot consolidation job? we rolled out a change to snapshot-merge yesterday that shifted windows to 03:00 for a region.

karen: yep, snapshot-merge cron was moved to 03:00 in eu-central to align with backups. That coincides with our local-gc job which kicks off heavy trim + compaction. bad overlap.

tom: overlap + per-host maintenance (fw-scan) likely saturated queue depth. if queue_depth is maxed, small random writes block and attach RPCs time out.

priya: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) pause snapshot-merge in eu-central for 30m (`snapshotctl pause --region eu-central --reason \"incident\"`), 2) lower local-gc concurrency: `localjanitor set-concurrency --region eu-central 1`, 3) bump attach retry window on kube-provisioner to tolerate transient latency.

arun: I'll pause the snapshot-merge now. applying `snapshotctl pause --region eu-central`.

infra-bot: action: snapshot-merge paused by arun at 03:08 UTC

zach: paused. I also throttled local-gc concurrency to 1 at 03:09. host IOPS dropped from ~120k to ~45k within 90s, p95 latency back to ~28ms. reattempting attaches.

tom: how many pending attaches?

zach: 56 pending, 41 succeeded after retry, 15 still failing and mostly pinned to 5 hosts (nvme0[12-16]).

karen: SMART doesn't show reallocated sectors. firmware scan returned OK. this looks like transient write-queue saturation exacerbated by compaction + snapshot churn.

priya: short-term runbook: 1) keep snapshot-merge paused for 1h, 2) keep gc concurrency at 1 for 30m, 3) evac the 5 worst hosts from new GPU allocs (cordon & drain gracefully).

arun: cordoning hottest hosts now: `kubectl cordon gn-euc-012 gn-euc-013 gn-euc-014 gn-euc-015 gn-euc-016` — draining next.

infra-bot: note: draining will reschedule Pods; expect ~2-3m per pod depending on image pull.

zach: after cordon/drain, attach failures drop dramatically. we succeeded 12/15 remaining attaches; 3 still flapping, investigating IO sched stats on those boxes.

tom: follow-up actions: - schedule snapshot-merge to off-peak window (04:30-05:30) and avoid overlapping with local-gc; - add a fast-path to preempt local-gc when attach latency >50ms; - add dynamic per-host gc caps based on real-time attach latency.

karen: also evaluate whether the firmware health scan can be staggered rather than all hosts at once; it bumps internal flash GC and causes write amplification.

priya: cost/ops tradeoff note: moving snapshot-merge later reduces interference but increases backup retention overlap with business window. ops to discuss with backups team. We should track MB written per merge vs attach failures to quantify impact.

arun: I'll open a follow-up ticket: \"avoid merge+local-gc overlap — dynamic gv2 scheduling\" and include graphs (nvme_iops, attach_latency, queue_depth, smart_stats).

zach: logging the incident: 03:02-03:45 UTC, root cause: scheduled compaction + snapshot-merge + firmware scan overlapping -> NVMe queue saturation -> GPU attach RPC timeouts. mitigations applied: paused merge, throttle gc, cordon hot hosts.

priya: plan to run a staging chaos test: simultaneously trigger snapshot-merge + local-gc + fw-scan against a small pool and confirm autoscaler/backoff behavior. this should be a required test before changing snapshot windows.

karen: good. will also add a metric-driven guard in the provisioning flow: if nvme_attach_p95 > 40ms then suspend new allocate routes to that host until recovered.

tom: thanks team. keep this thread updated if any host shows renewed latency after we re-enable jobs. :eyes:
